Subject: Q2 readiness — unblock register & exec ask tracker

Team — kicking off a focused thread to capture the outstanding asks from last week's cross-functional sync and to surface anything that needs an exec decision ahead of the QBR. I attached an initial unblock register (spreadsheet) with rows for product asks, roadmap exceptions, and external commitments. Please do the following before EOD Thursday: 

- Review ownership column and update % complete.
- Mark any item that requires an exec decision with "EXEC" and add a 1-line justification.
- For items tied to Nimbus (their QBR is next Thurs), include the exact metric they care about.

Quick background: Nimbus is asking for production latency P95 guarantees on their high-throughput routes and an uplift plan if we miss their Q2 SLA. We need consolidated asks + an explicit canary/fallback approach for the exec review.

Attachments: Q2-readiness-unblock-register.xlsx (sheet: open_asks)

Thanks — Markus

Thanks Markus — I updated the sheet with current status. Highlights: 

- PRD-114 (prompt tuning rollout) — owner: lauren_bishop — 60% complete. Blocker: infra for A/B routing (needs dedicated pool config). Marked as EXEC because it affects Nimbus behavior routing.
- ROADMAP-EXC-9 (delayed quantization schedule) — owner: karthik_iyer — deferred; added rationale and customer impact (cost delta).
- EVAL-72 (regression alert tuning) — owner: neha_kapoor — can be completed this sprint; no exec required.

Open question: do we want to trade a small cost increase for immediate latency stability (two-week dedicated capacity reserve) or push a canary? I put a note in the drive doc with both options and estimated $/month. Link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cQ2Readiness

Lauren

Appreciate the clear callouts. A couple quick technical clarifications we need from product before we can scope the canary plan: 

- Which exact routes will Nimbus consider high-throughput? We need the endpoint names + 99th percentile token lengths to size the KV/cache.
- If we do a dedicated capacity reserve, what's the SLA bump target (P95 target today vs requested)? Put numbers in the sheet and we can run a cost simulation (PRODOPS-737).

Proposed fallback: roll forward an acceleration config (lower quantization sensitivity for the critical route) for the canary window, monitor quality with the existing eval set, rollback automatically if Rouge-like metric drops >2 pts. I added a row in the unblock register and assigned myself as owner for runbook updates.

Vivek
Lead, Serving Runtime

Thanks for the quick turn. Finalizing action items for the exec packet — please treat this as the single source of truth and update the unblock register live. I pulled the highest-priority rows into the exec slide deck. Summary and owners: 

1) PRD-114 (prompt tuning A/B route) — Owner: Lauren Bishop — ACTION: confirm dedicated pool config or commit to canary by 2028-03-26. Marked EXEC.
2) INF-502 (runtime fallback plan & runbook) — Owner: Vivek Kulkarni — ACTION: publish runbook + rollback thresholds; runbook link and smoke test checklist due 2028-03-25.
3) ROADMAP-EXC-9 (quant schedule delay) — Owner: Karthik Iyer — ACTION: provide revised timeline and customer impact statement by 2028-03-25.
4) EVAL-72 (regression alert tuning) — Owner: Neha Kapoor — ACTION: complete tuning and provide validation results (pass/fail) by 2028-03-25.
5) Nimbus alignment doc — Owner: Marissa Cole — ACTION: confirm whether Nimbus will accept canary+fallback or require guaranteed P95. Marissa to confirm with Sanjay and update row.

Notes: I will escalate any unmet EXEC flags to the leadership QBR pre-read on Monday morning. If anyone thinks an item shouldn't be promoted to exec (or can be resolved by ops without a decision), flag it in the sheet and add a 1-line rationale.
